sources.title: 5.13 supervised targets, Linear costs and TinyLM parameter derivation
sources.details:
5.13 fresh arithmetic derivation, inspected and executed by /root/technical_dep_513.

Toy effective supervision: batch_size * targets_per_record * updates.
4 * 8 * 100 = 3200. Distinct records (16 or 64) do not change this product.
If each of the four records supplies four targets, 3200 / (4 * 4) = 200 updates.
Keeping 100 updates gives 4 * 4 * 100 = 1600 targets.
The audit executes the original Python fence and changes only the width8/records16 cell for both exercise cases.

Dense Linear: y_h = sum_(d=1..D) A_(h,d) x_d + b_h; weight shape H by D.
A common multiply-accumulate convention counts 2 operations per input-output pair.
Thus leading forward cost is approximately 2 D H per position: 2*8*8=128, 2*16*16=512; ratio 4.
An exact minimal nonbiased dot product uses D multiplications and D-1 additions per output.
The textbook says approximately and explicitly excludes bias and other costs, so it does not claim these are exact instruction counts or a complete Transformer training FLOP count.

Default one-layer TinyLM parameter count, vocab264, position128, untied embeddings, LayerNorm, GELU DenseFFN, one attention head:
Fixed input/output: embedding264w + position128w + output264w + final LayerNorm2w = 658w.
Attention Q/K/V/output: 4w^2 with no bias.
DenseFFN up/down: w*(4w) + (4w)*w + 4w + w = 8w^2 + 5w.
Two block LayerNorms: 4w.
Total P(w)=12w^2 + 667w.
P(8)=6104; P(16)=13744; P(32)=33632.
These counts were checked by constructing actual current TinyLM instances on PyTorch 2.14.1+cpu.
They measure parameter storage elements, not quality, actual runtime, or complete training memory.

Formal experiment supervision uses each ASCII UTF-8 byte plus EOS as a next-token target; BOS supplies only an input and padding labels are -100.
At seed42, family split: 64 train / 8 validation / 8 test; reconstructed JSONL SHA256 matches all three formal manifest hashes.
Whole-dataset mean denominators: 16-record training subset553; 64-record training2200; validation274; test276.
150 updates * batch4 = 600 draws, with replacement, separately from model initialization RNG.
Mean exposures per distinct training record: 600/16=37.5 vs 600/64=9.375.
Reexecuting only sampling and target counting yields 20765 for 16 records and 20623 for 64, for either model width; sampled target lengths are33,34,35.
This is supervised exposure, not the number of unique collected tokens.
For each stored validation and test result, nll_sum / effective_tokens agrees with nll to absolute tolerance1e-14.
The twelve displayed losses match the formal report to five decimal places (absolute rounding tolerance0.000005).
Training final_loss is fit_lm's full-dataset _nll after optimizer updates, not the last sampled batch history loss.
No optimization, GPU benchmark or training was rerun in this review.
